title: One screen for the whole SIEM
text: The Overview answers the daily questions in seconds: is every log source reporting, how busy is the SIEM, is anything being flagged, and are logs arriving on time.
spots: Sources that reported in the last 10 minutes. Silent sources are named here the moment they stop.
Events stored in the period, the change against the previous period and the peak rate.
Alerts by severity. Click for the filterable alert list.
How fresh the newest event is. Click for the delay per source.
UTMStack's own database health. Click for a plain-language explanation and the fix.
Live, 1 h, 6 h or 24 h for the counters, donut, rules and alert list.
The rules raising the most alerts. Click one to open its alerts.

title: Live map of firewall traffic and attacks
text: Every connection the firewalls log is drawn as an arc to the remote city. Attackers found in server and Microsoft 365 logs are plotted too. Red is blocked, yellow is VPN, purple is Tor.
spots: Firewall, Microsoft 365, Google, Windows, Linux or syslog, or everything at once.
Only allowed or only denied traffic.
Isolate traffic from VPN ranges, Tor exit nodes or hosting providers.
Type 22, 3389 or any port to see where that traffic comes from and goes to.
The newest blocked connections, with VPN, Tor and hosting badges. Hover a row to find it on the map.

title: Tor and VPN traffic at a glance
text: Address lists for VPN providers, datacenters and Tor exit nodes are downloaded and refreshed automatically, so anonymised traffic stands out in its own colour.

title: Who is knocking on port 22?
text: A port filter turns the map into an exposure check: every SSH attempt in the last minute, where it came from and which site it targeted.

title: Street-level context
text: Zoom in and a street map appears beneath the arcs. IP location is city-level, so this adds context rather than pinpointing a building.

title: Click an attacker: every port it tried
text: One click on a blocked connection shows what that address did in the last 24 hours: the ports it tried with their service names, how many were denied or allowed, the sites and addresses it reached, then reputation and WHOIS. Late replies to your own connections are counted apart, so the list shows real attempts only.
spots: Connections, denied vs allowed, first and last seen, and the ports tried on your side.

title: From a rule to its alerts in one click
text: Filter alerts by severity, source, rule or free text, and page through the history.
spots: One data source or all of them.
Free text across alert names, descriptions and addresses.

title: Alert detail with a recommended action
text: Each alert explains what happened and what to do, in plain language, with every stored field, live IP reputation from AbuseIPDB and VirusTotal, and WHOIS for each public address.
spots: Rule, severity, status, MITRE ATT&CK technique and the affected site.

title: Every data source, and when it last reported
text: Event counts, share, a 24-hour sparkline and status per source. Switch to By type to compare firewalls, servers and cloud.

title: One source in depth
text: Event history, the alerts the source raised and its most recent raw events.

title: Are logs arriving on time?
text: The delay between a device logging an event and UTMStack storing it, per source, with an explanation of what is normal.

title: SIEM health in plain language
text: When OpenSearch turns yellow or red, the panel says whether data is at risk, why, and the exact commands that fix it. Copy diagnostics gives your support provider everything at once.

title: Fix a yellow SIEM with one click
text: When OpenSearch turns yellow because of replica copies a one-server cluster can never place, enter your password and press Apply fix. Each step is shown with its result. A separate, narrow account makes only these changes; it cannot read or delete data.

title: 30 days of history
text: Hourly history and daily and weekly comparisons, kept in the dashboard's own database because UTMStack keeps raw logs for about a day.

title: Reports for management
text: PDF and HTML reports on demand or every day: key figures, top rules, recent alerts with MITRE ATT&CK techniques, top blocked countries and storage health.
spots: A report for the last 24 hours, ready in seconds.

title: Reports ready for management
text: Every report carries the logo and the copyright notice on each page, opens with key figures and plain-language key findings, then covers alerts, blocked attackers and the ports they tried, and who connected to whom.

title: Your layout, your screens
text: Move and resize panels, add widgets and screens, and choose which screens rotate on the NOC wall. Save a layout as everyone's default, or keep it personal.
spots: A new tab with its own layout.
Include this screen in Wall-mode rotation.
Drag a panel by its handle.

title: Settings without a restart
text: Login, reputation API keys, support contact, map locations, AI-traffic hosts and the report schedule. Keys are write-only and never shown again.

title: Works on a phone
text: Panels stack on a small screen, and the map supports touch zoom and pan.
